maladroit

mal-uh-DROYT · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Maladroit is unskillful, clumsy, or ineffective.

His maladroit attempt to fix the leaking faucet left the kitchen floor covered in water.

Example

The maladroit apology only made things worse, since the speaker kept accidentally insulting the very people he was trying to comfort.

Maladroit describes a clumsy, poorly handled attempt at something -- physical, social, or verbal -- that ends up making the situation worse rather than better.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

clumsy: Clumsy is the everyday word for lacking grace -- tripping over a rug, knocking over a glass, blurting out the wrong thing. Maladroit means much the same but is formal and literary, and it usually judges how badly a particular attempt was handled rather than a person's general coordination.

bungling: Bungling means botching a task through sheer incompetence -- the bungled repair, the bungled robbery -- so it needs a job that was actually attempted and ruined. Maladroit covers the same gracelessness but reaches wider, taking in social and verbal missteps handled without skill.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

adroit: skillful with hands or mind

graceful: smooth and skillful in execution

Where it sits · how total the clumsiness becomes

awkward → maladroit → hopeless

awkward vs. maladroit: An awkward moment just feels a little uncomfortable for a second; a maladroit attempt goes further, actively mishandling something and making the situation worse.

hopeless vs. maladroit: A hopeless attempt goes beyond even maladroit fumbling into total failure -- not just handled badly, but with no chance of success at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — mal-: badly (Latin (malus))

root — adroit: skillful (French (a droit, "properly"))

Put it together: mal- ("badly") + adroit ("skillful") = badly skillful -- clumsy or ineffective.

Use the root in a new word: direct: Everyone at the workshop wanted the bench beside the adroit old tailor.

Root Check

Word Choice

Maladroit is a somewhat formal, literary word -- in casual conversation, 'clumsy' is far more natural, but maladroit fits well in careful writing or a pointed critique.
